name: io.github.reeinharddd/snapmcp
description: Visual capture MCP server: terminal colors, code, diffs, PDFs, GIFs. 13 tools, SSRF on by default.

environmentVariables.name: SNAPMCP_THEME
environmentVariables.description: Shiki syntax highlighting theme (27 built-in: dracula, nord, catppuccin-mocha, tokyo-night, github-dark-dimmed, etc.). Auto-detects terminal theme when unset.

environmentVariables.name: SNAPMCP_FORMAT
environmentVariables.description: Output image format: png or jpeg

environmentVariables.name: SNAPMCP_QUALITY
environmentVariables.description: JPEG quality (1-100, only used for JPEG)

environmentVariables.name: SNAPMCP_SHADOW
environmentVariables.description: Drop shadow level: none, soft, medium, strong (aliases: sm, md, lg)

environmentVariables.name: SNAPMCP_ALLOWED_PATHS
environmentVariables.description: Comma- or semicolon-separated allowlist of file paths readable by capture_file (deny-all when unset)

environmentVariables.name: SNAPMCP_SSRF_PROTECTION
environmentVariables.description: Block requests to private IP ranges (DNS-resolved, IPv4 + IPv6). Default: true

environmentVariables.name: SNAPMCP_CHROME_EXECUTABLE
environmentVariables.description: Path to a system Chrome/Chromium binary to use for browser captures

environmentVariables.name: SNAPMCP_CHROME_PROFILE
environmentVariables.description: Chrome profile directory to use for browser captures (persistent context with cookies/extensions)

list.name: capture_terminal
list.description: Generate a styled terminal screenshot from text lines with real terminal theme colors. Auto-detects Kitty, GNOME, Alacritty, WezTerm themes for authentic prompt colors. Max 1000 lines.

list.name: capture_code
list.description: Generate a syntax-highlighted code screenshot using Shiki (50+ languages, 27 themes). Renders with line numbers, theme-aware colors, optional window chrome. Max 200KB input.

list.name: capture_browser
list.description: Take a screenshot of a URL using headless Chromium. Uses system Chrome profile when available for authenticated sessions. SSRF protection on by default. Full-page or viewport capture.

list.name: capture_file
list.description: Read a file and generate a syntax-highlighted screenshot with auto language detection from extension. Requires SNAPMCP_ALLOWED_PATHS allowlist. Max 5MB file size.

list.name: capture_markdown
list.description: Render Markdown as a styled document screenshot using GitHub-flavored Markdown. Supports tables, task lists, code blocks with syntax highlighting. Max 200KB input.

list.name: capture_html
list.description: Render arbitrary HTML as a screenshot with full CSS support. External scripts/iframes/stylesheets blocked for security. Max 200KB input.

list.name: capture_diff
list.description: Render a git diff with color-coded additions (green) and deletions (red). Parses unified diff format (git diff output). Max 500KB input.

list.name: capture_pdf
list.description: Convert a URL to a PDF document using headless Chromium. Full-page or viewport rendering. Uses system Chrome profile for authenticated pages. SSRF protection enabled.

list.name: capture_batch
list.description: Capture multiple items in a single call (max 10). Each capture uses typed parameters via discriminated union (terminal, code, file, browser, markdown, html, diff). Saves individual files.

list.name: capture_gif
list.description: Create an animated GIF from sequential captures (2-60 frames). Each frame uses typed capture parameters. Configurable frame delay (10-5000ms) and loop. Max canvas 8192x8192.

list.name: capture_sequence
list.description: Capture process steps as individual files + optional compiled GIF (max 60 steps). Each step has typed params plus stepNumber and label. Use for pipeline/tutorial visualization.

list.name: capture_document
list.description: Create a document (Markdown/HTML/PDF) with embedded step-by-step captures (max 30). Each capture has typed params and optional caption. HTML embeds images as base64; PDF is print-quality.

list.name: snapmcp-hint
list.description: Return contextual help for snapmcp configuration and usage. Topics: init, doctor, browser, themes, output, security, gif, document, batch.
